Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the InnoMed Devices Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Emily Carter, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are David Patel, CEO; John Ramirez, CFO; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; and Mark Levin, Chief Commercial Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to David Patel.

David Patel:
Thank you, Emily, and good morning, everyone. InnoMed Devices delivered strong results this quarter, driven by increasing adoption of our innovative medical devices and strategic partnerships.

Today, I will cover five key aspects of our performance:
1. FDA approvals and CE marks obtained
2. SG&A expense management and efficiency gains
3. R&D investment and innovation pipeline progress
4. Capital equipment vs consumables mix trends
5. Revenue and margin guidance for the next quarter/year

John will then provide a more detailed review of our financials. After that, we'll open the call for your questions.

Now, let's get started with our regulatory milestones. In the medtech arena, securing FDA approvals and CE marks is essential for unlocking market access, reimbursement pathways, and broad commercialization. This quarter marked significant progress in our structural heart and peripheral vascular franchises, where we achieved three FDA 510(k) clearances and one PMA approval, complemented by four new CE marks compliant with the EU MDR framework.

Leading the way in the US was the PMA approval for our EvoFlow™ Transcatheter Heart Valve, a next-generation self-expanding valve designed for high-risk patients with aortic stenosis. This approval follows our Breakthrough Device Designation from last year, backed by compelling results from the pivotal EvoFlow IDE trial—a multicenter, randomized study with 450 patients at 35 US and EU sites. The trial showed 98% procedural success, 95% one-year freedom from valve dysfunction, and a 2.5% annualized all-cause mortality rate, surpassing benchmarks from Medtronic's CoreValve and Edwards Lifesciences' Sapien platforms. We anticipate capturing 12-15% of the $4.2 billion US TAVR market by FY2026, with a Q4 launch targeting 25 leading centers such as Cleveland Clinic and Mayo Clinic.

Adding to this momentum, we secured 510(k) clearances for two peripheral vascular innovations: the FlexiStent™ Drug-Eluting Bioresorbable Scaffold for below-the-knee lesions in critical limb ischemia patients, and the PulseWave™ Peripheral Thrombectomy System, featuring AI-guided imaging that cuts distal embolization by 40% compared to Boston Scientific's AngioJet. Data from our PERSEVERE registry, involving over 1,200 patients, indicated 87% primary patency at 12 months for FlexiStent, tackling high restenosis issues in diabetic patients that challenge traditional metal stents. These advancements are set to grow our US vascular revenue from $180 million last year to more than $320 million in FY2025, a 78% CAGR, supported by new CMS reimbursement codes for BTK procedures.

Internationally, our four CE marks under the rigorous EU MDR—despite Notified Body delays affecting competitors like Abbott's Absorb GT1—include recertification for the CardioGuard™ Leadless Pacemaker with expanded MRI-conditional labeling up to 3T, plus Class III approvals for EvoFlow THV and the two peripheral products. This opens doors in key EU markets like Germany, France, and Italy, where structural heart procedures rose 22% year-over-year according to EFQM data, propelled by demographics and broader indications.

These wins are regionally transformative. In Europe, they fuel a full commercial ramp through our direct sales and Terumo Europe partnerships, aiming for €150 million in added sales over the next 18 months. We're preparing PMDA submissions in Japan next quarter for its $1.1 billion TAVR market with 30% penetration potential, and NMPA filings in China are progressing, with EvoFlow bridging studies matching local competitors like Peijia Medical.

Underpinning these successes is our $250 million R&D reinvestment over two years, centered on bioresorbable platforms—our PLLA-magnesium hybrid degrades 30% faster than Abbott's tech—AI/ML for 25% less fluoroscopy time, and modular designs slashing 510(k) timelines to 7 months versus the 11-month industry average. Our pipeline boasts 12 clinical programs, including a De Novo for NeuroPulse™ DBS in Parkinson's tremor patients, with Phase II data at 85% UPDRS-III improvement at 24 months, competitive with Medtronic's Percept PC. Four more FDA decisions are due year-end, with our 90% approval history intact.

Overall, these regulatory achievements de-risk growth, supporting 25% organic revenue for FY2025 and gross margins to 72%, with 18% quarter-over-quarter booking increases from KOLs and resolved supply chains via US nitinol sourcing.

Now, let's talk about SG&A expense management and efficiency gains. In our industry, competing against giants like Medtronic in CRM and Boston Scientific in peripherals, SG&A often hits 28-35% of revenue due to sales forces, compliance, and global ops. We've prioritized structural efficiencies, delivering Q3 SG&A at 29.2% of revenue—down 210 basis points year-over-year and 80 basis points sequentially—equating to $68 million in savings on 8% revenue growth to $1.25 billion. This boosted adjusted operating margin by 320 basis points to 22.4%, aligning with our full-year 22-23% target.

Our 'Elevate Efficiency' program, in year three, has yielded over $250 million cumulatively, targeting 6-8% annual SG&A reduction as a revenue percentage through 2026. This reallocates to high-ROI areas like TAVR and neuromodulation amid value-based care and CMS scrutiny.

Sales force optimization drove 45% of savings: With 4,500 global reps for products like Embla valves and NeuroStim DBS, we cut territory overlap 15% using Salesforce Einstein and Veeva CRM analytics, akin to Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci approach. Rep productivity rose 12%, revenue per rep to $1.2 million from $1.05 million. Shifting 25% of engagements to virtual via MediCore Connect saved $22 million in travel, leveraging US (62% revenue) for 250 bps leverage and offsetting Europe FX headwinds.

Procurement and back-office automation contributed 30%: SAP Ariba consolidated vendors from 1,200 to 850, saving 11% on $450 million indirect spend. UiPath RPA cut invoice cycles 40% and headcount 8% in Manila/Hyderabad centers, echoing Abbott's post-St. Jude model.

Marketing rationalization added 25%: Post-pandemic cuts of 20% in shows/events shifted to digital like LinkedIn and Virtual OR, boosting leads 18% at 60% less cost. Single ERP harmonization saved $15 million in legacy maintenance.

Regionally, US SG&A fell to 31% from 33.5% via GPO contracts with Vizient/Premier amid orthopedics competition; EMEA to 27% via Dublin hub navigating MDR; APAC at 35% for China Watchman LAAO ramp but improving ex-FX; LATAM with 10% savings.

We're reinvesting 60% of gains—$40 million this quarter—into AI robotics and biosensors for MACRA/IVDR shifts. Targeting under 27% SG&A by 2026, stress-tested for reimbursement cuts or tariffs, maintaining 20%+ margins. This builds sustainable leverage.

Moving on to R&D investment and innovation pipeline progress. R&D is our North Star for differentiation in structural heart, neuromodulation, and robotics against Intuitive and Boston Scientific. Q3 spend was $162 million, or 14.2% of $1.14 billion revenue—up 18% YoY, above Deloitte's 10.5% median and Abbott's 12.9%. Trailing 12 months: $628 million, 13.8% of sales, fueling 6-8% device CAGR per Grand View amid aging populations and outpatient shifts.

Returns are proven: Pipeline launches like drug-coated balloons and smart implants added $180 million incremental revenue, with $1 R&D yielding $4.20 lifetime value.

Our 28 active programs—92% milestones hit—span cardiovascular (45%), orthopedics/spine (30%), neuromodulation (15%), diagnostics/robotics (10%). Cardiovascular leads with VitalFlow TAVR 2.0 (24Fr sheath, AI deployment, <2% leak vs. Medtronic's 4-5%): IDE enrollment complete (850 patients), superior VARC-3 outcomes, PMA Q4 2024, CE Mark launched in Germany/France ($12M early revenue), China NMPA advancing. VitalResorb Gen3 coronary scaffold: 400-patient trial vs. Xience, 85% TLF-free, PMA mid-2025.

Orthopedics: CoreFlex Robotic Platform (haptic, 5G proctoring) IDE >300 cases, 22% faster procedures; OrthoSense AI implants 30% faster recovery, 18% ASC share.

Neuromodulation: VitalStim Pro DBS (62% UPDRS improvement vs. Medtronic), PMA Q1 2025; VisionAI OCT diagnostics CE/510(k), 12% UK share.

60% spend on US/EU, 22% APAC (Shanghai hub +45 engineers), LatAm localization. M&A like NeuroVive, NVIDIA partnerships cut timelines; hedged components. FY25 R&D 14-15% ($700M) for nanoparticles, CGM, AR endoscopy; $450-550M peak sales by 2027.

Next, capital equipment vs consumables mix trends. This mix signals profitability and recurring streams. Q3 revenue $1.28 billion, up 14% organic: consumables 68% ($872M, +18% YoY), capital 32% ($408M, +8%). T12M: 66% consumables from 58% two years ago, via 16% installed base to 4,200+ systems, 285 hours utilization (+11% YoY) via ApexLink 2.0.

US (52% revenue): 72% consumables (+22%), ASCs 28% placements, CMS boosts. Europe (28%): 64% (+12%), bundles offset DRGs. APAC (20%): 62% mix, 30% consumables growth, localization.

Pillars to 70/30 by 2025: Apex ProGen launch (350 units, $2.5M consumables each), BioSeal (+24% to $210M, 92% penetration), EndoVance M&A. FY25 consumables 20%+, recurring 72% at 85% margins.

Finally, revenue and margin guidance. For Q4 2024: $2.85-2.95 billion (+8-12% reported, 7-9% organic). Cardiovascular mid-single (US +12% TAVR, 150bps share EvoFlow 1,200 cases); Orthopedics high-single (Mako 1.5M procedures, China +20%); Neuromodulation double-digit (IntelliStim vs. Abbott). US 9-11%, Europe 4-6%, China/EM 15-18%. Gross margin 68.0-68.5% (+100bps, mix/supply), op margin 24.5-25.0%.

FY2025: $11.4-11.7 billion (8-10% organic). $1.2B launches (Aurora neuromod, FlexiStent), 100-200bps share, US 10%+, APAC 18-20%. Gross 68.5-69.0%, op 25.0-25.5%, EPS $8.75-9.00. Productivity $200M, M&A, sustainability.

I will now turn the call over to John Ramirez for a review of our financial results.

John Ramirez:
Thank you, David. As David highlighted, we delivered a strong financial performance this quarter. Q3 revenue reached $1.28 billion, up 14% organically, driven by procedural growth and mix shift. Gross margins expanded to 70.2%, reflecting premium products and supply efficiencies. Expenses were well-controlled, with operating income up 22% to $285 million. Adjusted EPS was $2.15, beating consensus. Balance sheet solid with $1.2 billion cash, supporting $500 million buyback authorization.

On profitability, our focus on leverage continues, with free cash flow at $210 million. For FY2024, we're raising revenue guidance to $5.1-5.2 billion and op margins to 23%.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Elena Vasquez for an update on our product pipeline.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, John. I'm excited to share updates on our innovative pipeline. We recently received FDA clearance for EvoFlow THV, a groundbreaking device that promises superior outcomes in TAVR procedures with reduced leak rates and high success metrics.

Building on David's overview, our pipeline advances include VitalFlow TAVR 2.0 on track for broader launch, CoreFlex robotics gaining ASC traction, and VitalStim DBS with strong clinical data. We're advancing 28 programs with high hit rates, new submissions for Aurora and FlexiStent, and regional expansions in APAC. These position us for $450-550 million peak sales.

Now, back to David for Q&A.

David Patel:
Thank you, Elena. Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for asking questions: Press star then one. Our first question comes from Sarah Thompson with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. David, on the recent FDA PMA for EvoFlow and the peripheral clearances, how do you see these impacting Q4 ramp and competitive positioning versus Edwards and Medtronic? Also, thoughts on EU MDR execution?

David Patel:
Great question, Sarah. The EvoFlow PMA is a game-changer, with IDE data showing clear superiority in procedural success and durability. We're targeting 25 top centers in Q4, projecting 12-15% TAVR share by FY2026. Peripherals like FlexiStent address BTK gaps, with PERSEVERE data driving 78% vascular CAGR. In EU, MDR CE marks despite backlogs unlock €150M via Terumo partnerships, with PMDA and NMPA next. We're outpacing peers on timelines thanks to modular designs and AI integration.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Lerner with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Lerner:
Thanks. John, your SG&A leverage was impressive at 29.2%. Can you talk more about sustainability, especially sales force productivity and regional differences? Any risks to the 27% target by 2026?

John Ramirez:
Absolutely, Mike. The 210bps YoY drop came from Elevate Efficiency: sales optimization lifted rep revenue 12% to $1.2M via analytics, virtual shifts saved $22M. Procurement via Ariba 11% savings, RPA headcount cuts. US to 31%, EMEA sharpest deleverage. Reinvesting 60% into R&D. Risks like inflation stress-tested; we'll hit under 27% with mid-single growth, maintaining 20%+ margins.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
Hi team. Mark, on consumables mix hitting 68%, how is commercial execution driving utilization, especially in US ASCs and APAC? Guidance impact?

Mark Levin:
Thanks, Lisa. Consumables +18% to $872M on 16% base growth, 285 hours utilization via ApexLink. US ASCs now 28% placements, CMS tailwinds to 310 hours. APAC 30% growth via JVs, localization. Bundles like EuroHeart secure commitments. This pushes to 70/30 FY25, de-risking with 85% margins; baked into Q4/FY25 organic guide.

David Patel:
Thank you for that insight, Mark.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Reilly with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Tom Reilly:
Congrats. Elena, R&D at 14.2% is aggressive—pipeline risks like PMA delays for VitalFlow or VitalStim? How does M&A/NVIDIA fit?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Good point, Tom. 92% milestones hit, 95% approval track. VitalFlow IDE superior, PMA Q4; VitalStim 62% UPDRS beat Medtronic. NeuroVive M&A adds programs, NVIDIA cuts timelines 18 months. FY25 $700M sustains, hedging supply. Positions for 25-30% EBITDA on launches.

David Patel:
Thank you for your questions. Before we conclude, I want to thank our employees, customers, and partners for their continued support. We are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders.

Thank you for joining us today.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
